To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the first examples of heterotrimetalic [(GdNi)(2) Ru] and [(DyNi)(2)RU] complexes have been prepared and magneto-structurally characterized.
we have prepared the first examples of pentameric [(LnNi)( 2)Ru] complexes with a high-magnetization ground state, which were characterized by X-ray crystallography and magnetostructural studies.

we have prepared and magneto-structurally characterized the first examples of heterotrimetalic [(LnNi)((2))Ru] complexes with a ferromagnetic ground state, which is rare for heterotrimetalllic systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of heterotrimetalic (Ln(III)-Ni(II)-Ru(III)) complexes.

the synthesis, characterization, and magnetism of new diphenoxo- and diphenoxylithio-bridged NiLn dinuclear complexes, which can be considered as platforms for the preparation of new heterotrimetalic [(Ni)(2)LnRu] complexes.
the synthesis of novel heterometallic compounds and their structural and magnetic characterization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic properties of these heterotrimetalics are dominated by the ferromagnetic exchange between the two Ni(II) ions, which is mediated by the Ln(III) ion.
the magnetic coupling in the heterotrimetalic complexes [(LnNi)((2))Ru] [Ln (3+) = Gda and Dya] is ferromagnetic and the ground state has a high magnetic moment, as predicted by the magnetic model.
the diphenoxo bridging unit is a good candidate for promoting ferromagnetic exchange interactions in dinuclear and heterotrimetalic complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic coupling in the [(LnNi)((2))Ru] systems (Ln = Gd, Dy) is ferromagnetic, which is in contrast to the antiferromagnetic coupling found in the corresponding [(LnCu)(2)Ru](2+) systems.
the diphenoxo-bridge ligand is a versatile platform for the construction of heterotrimetalic systems with high-magnetic-moments.

we have shown that a diphenoxo-bridge between a Ln(III) and a Ni(II) center is a viable strategy to obtain high-moment ground states in heterotrimetalic complexes, which are of potential interest for applications in magnetic data storage and quantum information processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the diphenoxo-bridge motif, which was previously shown to be efficient for stabilizing heterotrimetalic systems in which the two magnetic ions are both lanthanides (Ln(III)Ln(III)Ln (III)), can also be used to prepare systems in which one metal ion is a lanthanide and the other two are transition metals.
the magnetic properties of the heterometallic systems are strongly dependent on their structural features.
the use of a diphenoxo bridge between two Ni(II) centers and the Ru(III) center is a powerful strategy to obtain high-spin ground states for the resulting heterotrimetalic complexes.
